meta.title: Primordial Paradox action recipes: bullet board, i-frames, mercy, rule changes, jump, whip, knockback, fairness, boss phases
meta.citation_note: Every recipe cites source ids S1 to S9 from ACTION-MECHANICS.md section 1. Full titles, URLs and read dates live in that file and not here, because this directory is scanned by the project's clean-room gate.
meta.clean_room_note: No text, name, sprite or table from any commercial game is reproduced here. Facts about mechanics are described in our own words and expressed in our own numbers.
meta.arena: 160x100 box centred at 128,120; marker 8x8; 2 pixels per step

new_specs.title: action movement (jump, whip tiers, knockback, stairs, deep landing)
boss phases and rule changes (breakpoints, rule fields, interruption contract)

families.BRD: bullet board geometry and marker movement
families.MRC: mercy, ACT and non violent options
families.RUL: how a boss changes the rules of the board
families.JMP: the fixed jump arc and its landing
families.WHP: whip reach, whip timing and the upgrade gate
families.KNB: knockback arc and the lock that follows it
families.PHS: three phase boss structure and the interruption

recipes.name: Board box and dim
recipes.when_to_use: Every enemy turn in every battle. This is the stage the player is put inside, and nothing else draws there while it is up.
recipes.numbers: 160 x 100 box, 2 pixel ink frame plus a 1 pixel dark line outside, the rest of the field dimmed 60 percent black.
recipes.verify: The box edges land on whole pixels and the dim covers everything outside it.

recipes.name: Marker identity and trail
recipes.when_to_use: Always. The marker is the single highest contrast object on screen, so no hazard may share its palette.
recipes.numbers: 8 x 8 marker, 4 step trail, re-centres at the box centre at the start of every phase.
recipes.verify: The marker is findable in a still frame with the dim on.

recipes.name: Marker speed and wall clamp
recipes.when_to_use: Every phase, as the base rate the rule change fields may modify.
recipes.numbers: 2 pixels per step in 8 directions, clamped at the border with no jitter. Crossing the short side takes 50 steps, which is 0.83 s at 60 steps per second.
recipes.verify: Holding into a wall stops the marker on the border and does not flicker.

recipes.name: Hazard hitbox inset
recipes.when_to_use: Every hazard, so that a near miss reads as a near miss instead of a hit.
recipes.numbers: An 8 x 8 sprite carries a 4 x 4 hitbox, an 16 x 16 sprite carries 12 x 12, 2 pixels off per side.
recipes.verify: A hazard grazing the marker's corner does not register a hit in the preview room.

recipes.name: Reference scale against the studied board
recipes.when_to_use: Once, when arguing any change to box size, marker size or speed. It is the calibration recipe, not a runtime rule.
recipes.numbers: The studied board moves its marker at a hidden value of 4, raised to 5 (25 percent) for one boss. Ours crosses the short side in 50 steps, 0.83 s, so our box is relatively larger and our marker relatively quicker. That is the single biggest difficulty dial we own.
recipes.verify: Any request to enlarge the box or speed the marker is answered by this comparison first.

recipes.name: Slow key
recipes.when_to_use: Every phase. Hold cancel to halve the marker speed, so a bullet wall that already exists becomes a puzzle instead of a reflex gate.
recipes.numbers: 1 pixel per step while cancel is held, trail unchanged so the slower marker still shows intent.
recipes.verify: Holding cancel halves the crossing time and releasing restores 2 pixels per step in the same step.

recipes.name: 30 step invulnerability on hit
recipes.when_to_use: The default for every enemy turn. Applied by the arena, not by a pattern, so no recipe can shorten it.
recipes.numbers: 30 steps (half a second) of invulnerability after a hit. The marker blinks every 4 steps. An overlapping hazard cannot re-hit inside the window.
recipes.verify: Standing still inside a hazard stream costs exactly one hit per 30 steps.

recipes.name: Why 30 and not the studied 96
recipes.when_to_use: The written reason behind IFR-01, for the reviewer who asks why we did not copy the older game's window.
recipes.numbers: The older action game grants about 96 frames, 1.6 s, because its player has 64 hit points and healing items that cost no turn. Our player has 20 and enemy attacks of 2 to 6, so a 96 step window would let a player eat five hits for free.
recipes.verify: The arithmetic is stated in the spec so the number is argued, not assumed.

recipes.name: Relic that lengthens the window
recipes.when_to_use: One mid game relic. Makes invulnerability a stat the player can invest in, which is the alternative to a bigger health bar.
recipes.numbers: Plus 20 steps, so 50 total. Blink period tightens so the player can see the upgrade without reading a menu.
recipes.verify: With the relic equipped a standing player takes one hit per 50 steps in the same pattern.

recipes.name: Cadence gate for one optional fight
recipes.when_to_use: An optional superboss only. Never a story boss, never the last one, because the promise it breaks is the one the rest of the game keeps.
recipes.numbers: No invulnerability at all. Damage is refused on a fixed cadence of 4 steps instead, so the boss may be faster than the player but never hits twice in a step.
recipes.verify: In this fight a player inside a stream loses health at a fixed rate, and the rate is the same at every position in the box.

recipes.name: Clock starts on the hit
recipes.when_to_use: Always, and stated because the studied game does the opposite for a reason that does not apply to us.

params.studied_exception: stairs, where it starts at once

recipes.numbers: Our clock starts on the hit. The studied game starts it on landing because its hit ejects the player in a fixed arc that already removes control; we do not eject the marker, so a landing rule would hand out a fraction of the promised half second.
recipes.verify: Being hit at the top of the box gives the same 30 steps as being hit at the floor.

recipes.name: SPARE gate
recipes.when_to_use: Every fight in the demo must be openable by this gate, which is what makes the peaceful route real rather than decorative.
recipes.numbers: SPARE unlocks at trust 3 or at enemy HP of 25 percent or less, whichever comes first.
recipes.verify: Three TALKs then SPARE ends the same fight that a FIGHT chain would have ended.

recipes.name: Four TALK options that name a fear
recipes.when_to_use: Every boss and every enemy with a name. Each option is content, not a checklist item.

params.content_rule: the option that matters names something the enemy is afraid of

recipes.numbers: Up to 4 options, each adding 1 trust, none of them damaging. The rule that makes them read as an argument is that at least one names a fear in the enemy's own words.
recipes.verify: A reviewer can point at the option that carries the argument, and it is not the first one.

recipes.name: Visible refusal with a reason
recipes.when_to_use: Whenever SPARE is pressed and the gate is not met. A silent no-op is the failure this recipe exists to prevent.

messages: this one does not accept it yet

recipes.numbers: Second ink, one low blip, one line naming the gate and the current value. The turn does not advance.
recipes.verify: Pressing SPARE too early leaves the menu open and prints the number that is missing.

recipes.name: Repeated spare on one boss
recipes.when_to_use: Hector only. One fight where peace asks for nerve rather than bookkeeping.
recipes.numbers: Two spares in a row. A TALK between them is allowed but resets nothing, so the requirement is nerve, not arithmetic.
recipes.verify: One spare leaves Hector fighting; two in a row ends the fight with the peaceful victory text.

recipes.name: Deleted mercy on the last boss
recipes.when_to_use: Kronos on the blooded and genocide routes, until the kill condition is met. The opposite entry is refused with a flag, not with a trust count.

params.refusal: the entry draws disabled and the reason is spoken once

recipes.numbers: SPARE and TALK both draw disabled while the flag holds, and the director records the refusal in the ledger so the ending can account for it.
recipes.verify: On the mercy route Kronos still accepts a peaceful end; on the blooded route the entry is visibly dead.

recipes.name: One exception, flagged in data
recipes.when_to_use: At most once in the demo. An enemy that cannot be spared needs an explicit flag, and the ledger still records it.

params.ui: SPARE draws disabled from the first turn

recipes.numbers: 0 or 1 enemies in the demo. A disabled entry from the first turn reads as a fact about the enemy, not as a bug.
recipes.verify: The checker refuses a data file with more than one unsparable enemy in the demo.

recipes.name: One rule change per phase
recipes.when_to_use: Every boss with more than one phase. The phase may not introduce a new rule and a new hazard shape at the same time.
recipes.numbers: At most one of the two per phase, and the rule change is labelled for 24 steps inside the 12 step warning window.
recipes.verify: Reading a boss's phase table, no row shows both a new shape and a new rule.

recipes.name: Gravity board
recipes.when_to_use: Once in the demo, on a boss who fights by pinning the player down. The marker falls and a jump input lifts it.

params.direction: floor, or all four on the harder variant

recipes.numbers: The marker accelerates downward at 0.25 pixels per step squared, capped at 4, and the jump input lifts it 3 pixels of impulse.
recipes.verify: A player who does not press jump rests on the floor within 40 steps and never leaves the box.

recipes.name: Track board
recipes.when_to_use: One phase, where the boss wants the player to plan rather than react. The marker moves along lines and the perpendicular input switches line.
recipes.numbers: 3 horizontal lines 30 pixels apart, 2 pixels per step along the line, 3 steps to switch. No diagonal movement and no slow key.
recipes.verify: A pattern with a moving gap is clearable in 3 straight runs, one per line.

recipes.name: Shield board
recipes.when_to_use: The one phase where the player cannot move. It works only when the hazards come to a fixed point and the whole skill is timing.
recipes.numbers: No movement. Holding cancel raises a 24 pixel shield for up to 6 steps, then a 6 step cooldown. The phase is capped at 300 steps.
recipes.verify: A careless player and a careful player take visibly different damage in the same pattern.

recipes.name: Shooter board
recipes.when_to_use: The one phase that is a reward, not a test. Confirm fires a shot that removes a hazard, so the player who has learned the patterns gets to answer.
recipes.numbers: A 4 pixel per step shot with a 10 step cooldown, destroying one hazard per hit. The clear condition still waits for the pattern to end.
recipes.maps_to: NEW spec 18 (field hazard_mode = shooter), NEW spec 17 (confirm button)
recipes.verify: A player who fires steadily takes no damage in a pattern the same player could not dodge.

recipes.name: Inverted horizontal
recipes.when_to_use: Hector phase 2 only, for one phase, with the on screen direction arrow flipped so the joke is fair.
recipes.numbers: Left and right swap for the length of one phase. The label shows for 24 steps and a small flipped arrow sits in the corner while it holds.
recipes.maps_to: NEW spec 18 (field invert), spec 08 warning window
recipes.verify: The phase after it restores normal controls without a press, and the debug label says so.

recipes.name: Two markers, one input
recipes.when_to_use: Kronos final phase on the blooded and genocide routes only. The one place where the peaceful and violent paths play differently by rule.

params.mirror: point symmetry through the box centre

recipes.numbers: Two 8 x 8 markers mirrored through the centre, moved by one input, sharing one health pool. Both must survive the phase.
recipes.verify: The arena's hit test applies to both markers and a single hit costs one attack value, not two.

recipes.name: Committed fixed arc
recipes.when_to_use: Every jump in the action segments. One arc, no air control, no variable height, so a gap is a yes or a no.
recipes.numbers: 4 steps of startup, 40 steps in the air to flat ground, apex 42 pixels, horizontal speed fixed at takeoff. Walking horizontally it covers 40 pixels of ground, 2.5 blocks.
recipes.verify: A recorded input sequence jumps the same distance twice in a row, and holding the button does not go higher.

recipes.name: Landing table
recipes.when_to_use: Level design and the checker. The table is how a script proves a gap is clearable by exactly one jump.
recipes.numbers: Landing 2 blocks higher ends the jump at step 29, 1 block higher at 36, level at 40, one lower at 42, two lower at 44, three lower at 46.
recipes.verify: A jump from each of the six heights ends on the listed step, measured in the debug overlay.

recipes.name: Why fixed and not variable
recipes.when_to_use: The written argument behind JMP-01, for anyone who asks for variable height later.
recipes.numbers: Two more forgiving models exist: variable height by switching gravity to about 3.5 times on release, and a takeoff scaled by ground speed. Both multiply the arcs a level designer must check, and this game is not a platformer first.
recipes.verify: The spec states the choice and the cost, so the decision can be reversed deliberately rather than by accident.

recipes.name: Walk speed and stairs
recipes.when_to_use: Every action segment. Stairs are a mode, not a slope, and they are slower on purpose.
recipes.numbers: 1 pixel per step walking, 0.5 on stairs, and the player cannot land on stairs. Crossing the 256 pixel frame on foot takes 4.3 s.
recipes.verify: Walking a flat room of 256 pixels takes 256 steps, and a jump from stairs lands on the floor below, never on the stair.

recipes.name: Deep landing stun, cancelable by a whip
recipes.when_to_use: Any fall of 4 blocks or more. The stun punishes a bad descent but a well timed attack cancels it, which is the studied game's best small mercy.

params.cancel: a whip started in the air that ends on the landing step

recipes.numbers: 10 steps of stun after a fall of 4 blocks or more, cancelled if the whip's last recovery step lands on the same step as the ground contact.
recipes.verify: Both outcomes appear in the debug room: no attack, 10 step lock; timed attack, control on the landing step.

recipes.name: Whip tier 1
recipes.when_to_use: The starting weapon and the whole of the first act.
recipes.numbers: 24 pixels of reach, 2 damage, 12 step animation with contact at step 8 and 4 steps of recovery after a hit.
recipes.verify: An enemy placed 24 pixels away is hit; at 26 pixels it is not.

recipes.name: Whip tier 2, damage without reach
recipes.when_to_use: The middle tier. Its whole point is that it is a damage tier, which is the shape the studied game has and most imitations lose.
recipes.numbers: 28 pixels of reach, only 4 more than tier 1, and damage 3. The player feels stronger without the fight becoming a different fight.
recipes.verify: The tier 2 enemy that took 4 hits now takes 3, and the spacing that worked at tier 1 still works.

recipes.name: Whip tier 3, the reach tier
recipes.when_to_use: The last tier, and the moment the corridor fights change from trading hits to spacing.
recipes.numbers: 48 pixels of reach, 3 blocks, damage unchanged at 3. The longer animation is the price: 14 steps, contact at 9.
recipes.verify: With tier 3 the player can hit a hazard sprite from outside its own attack range, which is the designed reward.

recipes.name: Attack timing budget
recipes.when_to_use: Every whip level. A miss costs the full animation, a hit costs the animation plus recovery, and that asymmetry is the combat.
recipes.numbers: A miss costs all 12 steps. A hit costs 12 plus 4 of recovery. The studied game spends 22 frames with contact at 17, which is why its fights are about spacing rather than mashing.
recipes.verify: Two attacks in a row are 16 steps apart after a hit and 12 apart after a miss, measured in the debug overlay.

recipes.name: Upgrade gate by hearts
recipes.when_to_use: The two upgrades, so a player who hoards hearts is rewarded and a player who spends them on subweapons is not punished twice.
recipes.numbers: 4 hearts for tier 2, 8 for tier 3, and the drop only appears when no subweapon is on screen. The level resets on death, which is the whole tension of the heart economy.
recipes.verify: A player with 3 hearts never sees the upgrade; the checker refuses a drop rule that ignores the subweapon condition.

recipes.name: Knockback arc
recipes.when_to_use: Every non fatal hit in the action segments. Not used in the arena, where the marker is not ejected.
recipes.numbers: 16 pixels away from the hit's side and 10 pixels up, travelling at the same 1 pixel per step as a walk. The arc ignores current momentum, so being hit mid jump drops the player out of the arc.
recipes.verify: A hit taken mid jump lands at the same distance from the attacker as a hit taken standing.

recipes.name: Direction from the hit's side
recipes.when_to_use: Always. The direction is a field, written by whoever applied the damage, not read from the player's facing.
recipes.numbers: One field with two values, written by the damage source. The studied third game keeps exactly this byte next to the wounded timer, which is the reason the trick of bumping into an enemy to gain height works there.
recipes.verify: A hazard behind the player pushes forward and a hazard in front pushes back.

recipes.name: No pit within one knockback
recipes.when_to_use: A level design check, run by script over every room with a hazard and a pit.
recipes.numbers: No pit edge within 16 pixels of a hitbox belonging to an enemy that survives one whip. A one whip enemy beside a ledge is not a challenge, it is a coin flip that looks like a mistake.
recipes.maps_to: NEW spec 17, spec 04 (rails and triggers), spec 15 (tiles)
recipes.verify: The room checker names the room, the tile and the enemy for every violation.

recipes.name: Label the rule change
recipes.when_to_use: Any phase where a rule changes (RUL-02 to RUL-07). A rule change the player cannot name will be read as a bug.
recipes.numbers: 24 steps of label inside the 12 step warning, one short phrase, no explanation. Six phrases total, one per rule.
recipes.verify: Every rule change in the enemy data resolves to one of the six phrases and the checker refuses an unlabelled one.

recipes.name: Never spawn inside the trail
recipes.when_to_use: Every pattern, as an extra exclusion on top of the 24 pixel rule.
recipes.numbers: The 24 pixel exclusion applies to the marker's position at spawn time and to the previous 4 steps, so a hazard cannot appear in the space the player just left.
recipes.verify: The pattern checker simulates each recipe and asserts no spawn inside the 4 step trail.

recipes.name: Pattern ends on its own length
recipes.when_to_use: Every pattern. A passive player must see the pattern finish, because a pattern that waits for the player is a stall, not a test.
recipes.numbers: The phase ends at the declared length plus the longest hazard life, capped at 900 steps, and plays the clear chime and 12 steps of text.
recipes.verify: Standing still in the preview room ends every pattern inside its declared length.

recipes.name: Three phase skeleton
recipes.when_to_use: Every boss with more than one phase: teach, change one rule, combine at speed.
recipes.numbers: Phase 1 from 100 to 70 percent teaches one shape. Phase 2 from 70 to 40 changes exactly one rule and adds one shape. Phase 3 from 40 to 0 keeps the phase 2 rules and raises speed to 1.25 times. 30 step break, no healing.
recipes.verify: Reading Percy's phase table, no phase adds both a rule and a shape, and the break is 30 steps.

recipes.name: Percy, the worked example
recipes.when_to_use: The first real fight, and the model every later boss is copied from.
recipes.numbers: 120 HP, attack 3 to 6, rain at 2 hazards, then wall at 3 with the box narrowed to 128 x 100, then fan at 3 with hazard speed at 1.25 times.
recipes.verify: Changing Percy's HP to 60 in data moves both breakpoints and needs no code edit.

recipes.name: Prometheus interruption at 40 percent
recipes.when_to_use: Once, in the Percy fight, and never in the arena code. It is a spec 06 scene that the battle hands over to.

params.branch: route flag: mercy and undecided vs blooded and genocide

recipes.numbers: The battle returns `interrupted` at 40 percent HP, which the checker treats as a resolved battle. The scene runs 4 commands plus a branch on the route flag, then sets the flag and returns control with no press.
recipes.verify: Both branches play when the flag is flipped, and an interrupted battle is not a checker error under spec 06 rule 6.

recipes.name: Hector two phases, Kronos four
recipes.when_to_use: The two bosses after Percy. Two phases is the shape players remember as a fight; four is only allowed at the end, and only on one route.

phases: two markers, blooded and genocide only

recipes.numbers: Hector: 2 phases, the second inverting the horizontal axis, and two spares in a row for the peaceful end. Kronos: 3 phases for everyone plus a 4 phase only where the ledger says blooded or genocide.
recipes.verify: On the mercy route the fourth Kronos phase is unreachable, and the checker refuses a route flag that would allow it.
